newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher, cement share soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher, cement share soars.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher for the third consecutive day led by a sharp move up in Cementos Rio Claro, a cement maker belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.57 percent at 13,592.08 on above-average trading volume of 6.02 billion pesos -- fueled by large cross trades including one involving Rio Claro.
Bogota's IBB index closed up 0.32 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 869.80 on a volume of 2.1 billion pesos.
Brokers in Medellin said trading was heavily concentrated in Rio Claro, which jumped 9.89 percent to end at 3,300 pesos per share on a cross in which 2.4 billion pesos of shares traded hands.

Ordinary shares of Banco Ganadero were also actively traded in Medellin, accounting for nearly 3.0 billion pesos of total volume. Ordinary shares in the bank, Colombia's largest in terms of assets, ended up 1.93 percent in Medellin at 290 per share.
Brewer Bavaria SA was among other gainers in Medellin, rising 3.15 percent to end at 3,920 pesos per share.
Cementos Argos, another cement manufacturer belonging to the Sindicato Antioqueno group, was among the winners in Bogota, rising 0.36 percent to close at 5,430 pesos a share.
Bavaria, one of the crown jewels of the group, ended at the same 3,920 peso level in Bogota where it gained 1.29 percent.

A recent drop in interest rates is seen as positive for stocks over the near-term. Some market analysts say talk of a possible improvement in U.S.-Colombian affairs, after the U.S. presidential election in November, could also help give Colombian stocks a lift.
